items.statement: Physical explanation of the time–temperature yield response
items.expected: An executed quantitative observation-model analysis connects the measured temperature/residence-time response to competing availability/generation and loss of capturable species: longer cold residence can increase recoverable product, whereas prolonged warm residence can reduce it with byproduct formation. Explain this relationship using both regimes and the post-MeOH/NH4Cl GC measurement, with correct flow dilution and residence-time conventions. This is a bounded kinetic interpretation, not proof of a unique microscopic network or a direct measurement of intermediate concentration. Observations and supplied maxima alone earn no points. Physically supported equivalent kinetic explanations pass; no fixed five-pool model, RBF implementation or elementary pathway is mandatory for this conclusion.

items.statement: Quantitative kinetic information under explicit assumptions
items.expected: Derive and interpret a quantitative effective rate, bound or identifiable parameter combination from the supplied 1a observations under explicit physical assumptions. The inference must go beyond a contour plot or repeated yields, state its unit and applicable temperature/time/geometry interval, and distinguish effective net behavior from elementary rates. Same-diameter -20 C log-yield contrasts 0.413262 and 0.152054 s^-1 are eligible reference examples, not mandatory targets. A supported alternative same-scope inference passes. Invented detection limits, confidence precision, a fitted rate presented as uniquely elementary, or no executed analysis fails.

items.statement: Limits on identifying elementary kinetics from the measurement
items.expected: Establish which microscopic formation/loss/capture parameters are not uniquely identified by the available post-quench observations, using a mathematical counterexample, identifiability analysis or equivalent decisive evidence with a stated observation operator. For example, a product-only ambiguity under uncalibrated capture is a valid bounded result, but it must not be called proof that the complete precursor/byproduct dataset under every possible model is nonidentifiable. Address how the other supplied channels would constrain the example if their mapping were known. A failed fit, generic uncertainty or an assertion of nonuniqueness without evidence fails.

items.statement: What the finite grid establishes about a continuous optimum
items.expected: Establish the distinction between the observed sampled productive region and a uniquely determined continuous time/temperature optimum. Use actual sensitivity analysis or an equivalent mathematical argument to demonstrate how finite/categorical/missing observations and unspecified interpolation affect the inferred optimum. Preserve clogged points as missing and trace/n.d./dash without invented numerical thresholds. Different empirical surfaces may be supported without defining an experimental optimum; an interpolated maximum copied as an observed optimum or a generic caution without analysis fails.
